label: General-Awareness Safety Net
blurb: A focused six-fact drill set for General-Awareness Safety Net.

topics.title: United Nations
topics.hook: The United Nations was founded in 1945 to promote international peace, cooperation, and development.
topics.explainer: The United Nations was founded in 1945 to promote international peace, cooperation, and development. It is a useful TCS Quiz recall point because questions often test the term, person, date, or application together.

connections.relationship: UN peacekeeping after the Suez Crisis
connections.fact: The UN General Assembly created the first United Nations Emergency Force after the 1956 Suez Crisis to supervise the end of hostilities and withdrawal from Egyptian territory.
The International Olympic Committee has held UN General Assembly observer status since 2009, and the Assembly regularly adopts an Olympic Truce resolution.

topics.title: Indian Constitution
topics.hook: The Constitution of India came into effect on 26 January 1950.
topics.explainer: The Constitution of India came into effect on 26 January 1950. It is a useful TCS Quiz recall point because questions often test the term, person, date, or application together.

connections.fact: The Constitution establishes India's republic; the Bharat Ratna is a civilian award created by government notification, not by a constitutional article.

connections.relationship: Domestic supreme law and international charter
connections.fact: India's Constitution governs the Indian state, while the UN Charter creates duties within an international organisation.

topics.title: Nobel Prize
topics.hook: The Nobel Prizes were established through the will of Alfred Nobel.
topics.explainer: The Nobel Prizes were established through the will of Alfred Nobel. It is a useful TCS Quiz recall point because questions often test the term, person, date, or application together.

connections.relationship: International prize and Indian civilian honour
connections.fact: Nobel Prizes follow Alfred Nobel's will and specified fields; the Bharat Ratna recognises exceptional service without being a Nobel category.

connections.relationship: Global recognition in scholarship and sport
connections.fact: Nobel laureates are selected for achievements in defined fields, while Olympic medals are won in international athletic competition.

topics.title: Olympic Games
topics.hook: The modern Olympic Games were revived in Athens in 1896.
topics.explainer: The modern Olympic Games were revived in Athens in 1896. It is a useful TCS Quiz recall point because questions often test the term, person, date, or application together.

connections.relationship: International achievement awards with different bases
connections.fact: Olympic medals reward sporting performance at the Games, while Nobel Prizes recognise work in fields named by Nobel’s will.

connections.relationship: Olympic Truce and UN observer status
connections.fact: The UN General Assembly supports the Olympic Truce, and the International Olympic Committee participates in Assembly work as a permanent observer.

topics.title: Suez Canal
topics.hook: The Suez Canal connects the Mediterranean Sea and the Red Sea through Egypt.
topics.explainer: The Suez Canal connects the Mediterranean Sea and the Red Sea through Egypt. It is a useful TCS Quiz recall point because questions often test the term, person, date, or application together.

connections.fact: The 1956 Suez Crisis led the UN General Assembly to establish the first United Nations Emergency Force for deployment in and around Egypt.

connections.relationship: Sadat’s canal reopening and peace diplomacy
connections.fact: Egyptian President Anwar Sadat reopened the Suez Canal in 1975 and later shared the 1978 Nobel Peace Prize for the Camp David peace framework.

topics.title: Bharat Ratna
topics.hook: The Bharat Ratna is India's highest civilian award.
topics.explainer: The Bharat Ratna is India's highest civilian award. It is a useful TCS Quiz recall point because questions often test the term, person, date, or application together.

connections.relationship: National honour outside the constitutional text
connections.fact: The award belongs to the Republic of India but was instituted by executive notification in 1954 rather than created by the Constitution.
Bharat Ratna recognises exceptional service in India; Nobel Prizes are international awards funded under Alfred Nobel's will.

questions.q: In which year was the United Nations founded?
questions.explanation: The UN was created in 1945 after the Second World War to support peace, cooperation, development, and international law.

questions.q: When did the Constitution of India come into effect?
questions.explanation: The Constituent Assembly adopted the text on 26 November 1949, but commencement occurred on Republic Day, 26 January 1950.

questions.q: Whose will established the Nobel Prizes?
questions.explanation: Alfred Nobel directed most of his estate to prizes in named fields, creating the basis for the international awards.

questions.q: Where were the first modern Olympic Games held in 1896?
questions.explanation: Athens hosted the first modern Olympics in 1896, reviving an international festival inspired by the ancient Greek Games.

questions.q: Which two seas does the Suez Canal connect?
options: Arabian Sea and Bay of Bengal
questions.explanation: The Egyptian canal links the Mediterranean with the Red Sea, shortening the Europe-Asia sea route by avoiding Africa's southern tip.

questions.q: What rank does the Bharat Ratna hold among Indian civilian awards?
questions.explanation: Instituted in 1954, the Bharat Ratna is India's highest civilian honour for exceptional service or performance.

questions.q: Which statement avoids confusing the UN with the Indian Constitution?
options: The UN is an international organisation; the Constitution is India's supreme domestic law
The Constitution created every UN agency
The UN administers the Bharat Ratna
questions.explanation: The UN Charter governs an intergovernmental body, while India's Constitution structures national government and rights within India.

questions.q: Which comparison with the Bharat Ratna is accurate?
options: Nobel Prizes are international awards; Bharat Ratna is an Indian civilian honour
Both were created by the Indian Constitution
Bharat Ratna follows Alfred Nobel's will
questions.explanation: The awards differ in origin, scope, and selection even though both recognise exceptional human achievement.

options: Opening of the Suez Canal in 1869
questions.explanation: The canal opened in 1869, followed by Athens 1896, the United Nations in 1945, and constitutional commencement in 1950.

questions.q: Which claim about the Bharat Ratna is incorrect?
options: It is India's highest civilian award
It was created by a specific article of the Constitution
questions.explanation: The government instituted Bharat Ratna by notification; no constitutional article creates the award.
